subject: Finovate bake-off recap & outstanding tests
body:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emily Santos <emily.santos@finovate.com>; Raj Patel <raj.patel@finovate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Finovate bake-off recap & outstanding tests

Hi Emily / Raj —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while items are fresh and to confirm the list of bake-off tests we discussed so your engineers can run the same bench in parallel. Summary below, followed by the open questions and next steps we committed to.

Key pain points you described
- Latency during peak batch windows (real-time chat use case; spikes causing UX delays)
- Unit cost of generation at scale — need clear cost projections against current spend
- Data residency & auditability for regulated financial workflows (SOC2, retention, SIEM hooks)
- Fragmented evaluation criteria across teams (ML, infra, security) — you asked for a compact decision matrix

Goals from the evaluation
- Demonstrate equivalent or better request latency at P95 for short replies (~<250ms target) under a realistic request mix
- Measure per-request cost using representative prompts (50k monthly active queries projected)
- Verify private deployment options (VPC + KMS) and evidence for SOC2 controls
- Validate model quality on your denial/edge-case prompts (hallucination and compliance-safe responses)

Bake-off test plan (agreed)
1) Latency & throughput: 1k concurrent short-chat sessions (avg 30 tokens), measure P50/P95/P99 and tail variability across 2-hour sustained run. Owner: Redwood Tech (Karthik).
2) Long-context handling: 2k-token context scenario with KV cache warm/cold runs; measure incremental cost and quality. Owner: Finovate Eng (Raj).
3) Cost run: run a mixed workload (chat + 1-shot summarization + embeddings) on identical prompts to compare $/1000 tokens. Owner: Finovate Eng (Emily) with our cost script.
4) Quality benchmark: your seeded prompt suite (50 prompts) with manual scoring for hallucination and compliance flags. Owner: Finovate ML (Emily + Raj) — scoring rubric shared in attachment.
5) Security/compliance checklist: we will provide detailed SOC2 evidence and an on-demand architecture diagram. Owner: Redwood security (Marissa).

Attachments included with this message:
- finovate_bakeoff_matrix.xlsx (cookbook + scoring sheet)
- redwood-performance-brief.pdf (short technical note on runtime, batching, and expected kernels)
- Finovate_RFP_202602.pdf (your original RFP for reference)

Open questions we promised to answer
- Can Redwood provide static egress IPs for your firewall allowlist? (answer pending)
- Exact behavior for model-version pinning & rollbacks during canary deployments — we will document interfaces.
- Any hard limits on retained KV cache size in Private deployment (impact on long-context cost).
- Confirmation of expected SLA for Dedicated pool vs hosted tier (requested by your infra).

Immediate next steps and owners (dates in PST)
- Karthik: share the Redwood workload driver + dockerized harness by Thu 2026-02-19 EOD.
- Emily/Raj: run baseline runs against CompetitorX and share their raw CSV export by Mon 2026-02-23.
- Marissa: send SOC2 control matrix and SSO/KMS docs by Fri 2026-02-20.
- Mina: draft commercial* assumptions and a 3-line pricing sketch for 50k MAU by Mon 2026-02-23.

*commercial sketch will be purely directional for bake-off; formal proposal follows once we have parity numbers.

If this looks right, please reply with any corrections and whether you want the Redwood harness to run from your env (we can run and share results) or you want us to provide an AMI/container to drop into your infra.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: finovate_bakeoff_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 72KB), redwood-performance-brief.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

-----Original Message-----
From: Emily Santos <emily.santos@finovate.com>
Sent: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:15:00 -0800
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finovate.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: initial demo + questions

Thanks Mina — this matches our notes. Two clarifications from our side:
1) For the latency run, can you also provide a breakdown by model variant (quantized vs float32)? We want to see the tradeoffs visually.
2) For compliance evidence, our audit team insists on encryption-at-rest screenshots and a sample logging trace that includes request IDs.

We can run CompetitorX on our cluster but will need the harness you mentioned. If you can provide an AMI/container with the harness that would speed things up.

Emily
Director of ML Platforms | Finovate Systems
--

On Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 13:50 Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick note — looping Marissa and Karthik for tech and security follow-through.
>
> Marissa: can you confirm the SOC2 artifact timeline and whether we can provide request-ID tracing screenshots?
> Karthik: I'll need the workload driver and the small config snippet for quant vs float runs by EOD Thu.
>
> Mina
>
-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Sent: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 12:08:00 -0800
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Santos <emily.santos@finovate.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@finovate.com>
Subject: Re: Finovate bake-off prep

Adding a couple notes from the product perspective:
- CompetitorX tends to have lower cold-start latency but higher steady-state cost because they don't support selective KV caching; include that as a row in the matrix.
- We should prioritize the long-context tests since Finovate has a lot of long ledgers in a single thread — our hybrid cache mode typically helps.
- For canarying, Redwood supports pinning model hashes per route; I'll attach the rollout example in a follow-up.

Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Console

--

[End of thread]
